thread:
Incident Bot: URGENT: Detected widespread token signature verification failures for Okta-issued tokens across api-*, console, and gateway. 401s spiking since 10:04 UTC. Auto-page -> SRE Oncall :rotating_light:
SRE Oncall: seeing it in prod metrics, auth-proxy 401 rate +350% since 10:04. console.login errors correlate. grabbing logs now.
Alex H: pushing stacktrace sample — auth-proxy log: `error=jwt_signature_invalid kid=gl-rotated-2026`. Okta JWKS fetch returned 500 for /oauth2/v1/keys at 10:03:58 in multiple regions.
Maria G: Okta status shows partial degradation for keys endpoint (https://status.okta.com/incidents/abc123). Looks like a bad JWKS rotation pushed malformed key.
Dave P: impact: internal console and API auth, customers on dedicated accounts report login failures. I'm seeing customer-support tickets: ~30 so far.
Alex H: reproduction curl (local):
```
curl -i "https://dev-123.okta.com/oauth2/v1/keys"
HTTP/1.1 500 Internal Server Error
{"error":"unexpected jwk format"}
```

Maria G: quick mitigation options: (1) fallback to cached JWKS (if present) and disable cache expiry for 1h, (2) switch verification to introspect endpoint (/introspect) for active tokens (costly), (3) allow legacy KID list from backup CDN snapshot (risky).
SRE Oncall: prioritize safest fast fixes: enable cached JWKS and route console auth to introspect for interactive logins only. That keeps API token verification strict.
Alex H: toggled feature flag `auth.proxy.use_cached_jwks=true` in prod-config-store (rollout 100%). Patch applied -> broadcasting to edge: `kubectl rollout restart deploy/auth-proxy -n prod`
Deploy Bot: deploy/auth-proxy restarted (3/3 pods) — restart time 10:12 UTC.
SRE Oncall: monitoring 401s...
Maria G: Okta support acknowledged via ticket OKTA-98765; they confirm bad rotation and are rolling back to previous key. ETA unknown.
Dave P: after cache flip we still see some 401s for new sessions. Console flows that require immediate verify still failing because session middleware does local signature verification before cached keys warmed.
Alex H: quick hotfix: adjust middleware to delay local signature verification for web sessions and call introspect instead. Pushing canary to web-auth path only.
Alex H: canary manifest snippet:
```
- name: web-auth-canary
  env:
    - AUTH_VERIFY_MODE=introspect-onboarding
```

Deploy Bot: deploy/web-auth-canary started (1/1) at 10:18 UTC.
Elena R: customer comms: drafting status update — short, include workaround (re-login after ~10-15m) and link to Okta status. Also note we're prioritizing enterprise customers with dedicated contacts.
Product Ops: add escalation note for accounts with SSO SLOs >99.9%. We'll create a targeted message to account managers.
SRE Oncall: canary looks good, console login failures down ~80% for canary traffic. Rolling this change to all web-auth pods.
Deploy Bot: deploy/web-auth rollout 50% -> 100% complete at 10:24 UTC.
SRE Oncall: global 401 rate trending down but still noisy. API clients with non-interactive tokens still failing where KID didn't match cached keys.
Alex H: for API traffic we dropped a short-term mitigation: accept introspect fallback for token validation on auth-proxy only if signature verification fails and introspect returns active=true. Implemented lightweight introspect fallback with circuit breaker to avoid blowing Okta.
Alex H: added rate-limit to introspect calls: 100rps global.
SRE Oncall: enabling now.
Maria G: Okta support update: they reverted the rotation at 10:30 UTC and are re-issuing stable keys. They expect full key endpoint recovery by 10:40 UTC.
SRE Oncall: seeing JWKS endpoint healthy from our side at 10:33. Pulling fresh keys and clearing disabled-cache flag.
Alex H: ran `curl https://dev-123.okta.com/oauth2/v1/keys` -> 200, valid keys returned. Triggered `auth-proxy` key reload API: `POST /internal/keys/reload` -> 200.
SRE Oncall: re-enabled strict verification for API traffic; introspect fallback disabled.
Dave P: customer-impact summary to share: ~30-60 minutes of login/API 401s for multi-org customers; console was partially degraded for ~20 minutes for many users. No data loss.
Elena R: posted status update for customers at 10:38 UTC: "We experienced intermittent login failures due to Okta JWKS rotation; issue mitigated. If you still see login problems please contact support. Link to Okta status: https://status.okta.com/incident/abc123"
Product Ops: alerted AMs for top 10 enterprise customers; scheduling follow-up.
SRE Oncall: handing off to morning oncall (Alex H) for postmortem and monitoring. @Alex H you'll take lead.
Alex H: ack. I'll collect logs, timeline, and runbook gaps. Initial action items: (A) add stricter JWKS validation in pre-prod to catch malformed rotations, (B) create automated warm failover to CDN-hosted JWKS snapshot, (C) document introspect fallback circuit breaker settings.
Incident Bot: INCIDENT RESOLVED by SRE Oncall at 10:40 UTC — status: mitigated, monitoring.
Elena R: adding flags: :white_check_mark: customer comms sent, :wrench: follow-up runbook tasks created, :clock1: postmortem assigned.
Dave P: creating internal ticket with impact metrics and list of affected customer IDs.
Alex H: dropping a sample log query for postmortem: `logs.app("auth-proxy") | where level=="error" and message contains "jwt_signature_invalid" | timeslice 1m | count()`
SRE Oncall: leaving monitoring on for 6 hours. Handing over to Alex H.
Alex H: thanks — will run a retrospective and propose runbook changes. Everyone reponded fast — good job. :clap:
